dateLabel: proposals range from 2.5 million to 60,000 years ago
title: How and when language began
summary: There is no scientific consensus on language's origin. Direct evidence is so scarce that many scholars view the topic as too speculative, and proposed dates span millions of years.
why: Language is arguably the defining human ability, and its birth left no fossils.
question: When and how did human language first emerge?
evidence: Proposed dates: Homo habilis (~2.5 Ma), Homo erectus (~1.8 Ma), Homo heidelbergensis (~600 ka), at least 100,000 years (Nichols), 200,000–60,000 years (Berwick and Chomsky).
wouldSettle: Converging evidence from genetics, fossil anatomy and archaeology tying speech capacity to a dated lineage.

theories.name: Continuity
theories.idea: Language evolved gradually out of earlier primate communication systems.

theories.name: Discontinuity
theories.idea: Language appeared relatively suddenly as a uniquely human trait.

theories.name: Gesture first
theories.idea: Language grew out of hand and facial gestures before speech.

theories.name: Vocal or song first
theories.idea: Language grew out of vocal sounds, often linked to early song.
